reduction_loops.doing_work_not_inert: chunk value is liveness-driven: budget = ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES // (m * itemsize * ff) = 245760 // (1*4*7) = 8777 -> prev_pow2 -> 8192, then min(LOOPED_CHUNK=16384, 8192) = 8192. A single-tile body (ff=1) would emit 16384; ff in {4..7} lands at 8192. The emitted _REDUCTION_BLOCK_1=8192 matches. So both the persistent->looped flip AND the specific chunk size are products of the liveness signal, not inert constants.

load_eviction_policies.status: coupled-side-effect-of-the-persistent-flip, NOT an inert field set by the lever
load_eviction_policies.detail: flj has num_load=2 (skips the num_load==1 stream branch) and row_reread=True. So when the liveness lever flips persistent->looped it ALSO causes load_eviction_policies to be set to ['last','first'x17] (reread pattern); in the persistent verdict the field is absent/default. Thus the EMITTED SEED differs in TWO fields (reduction_loops AND load_eviction_policies), not strictly one as the claim states.
load_eviction_policies.is_it_load_bearing_or_inert: INERT for the stated spill mechanism: n_spills is byte-identical (480 / 0) with reread vs default eviction. The eviction change is a mechanism-grounded HBM re-read hint coupled to the looped path (the looped body re-reads the row), confirmed not to affect register residency. It is a correct, deliberately-gated coupling, NOT dead weight to drop -- but it means the claim's 'exactly ONE structural field' phrasing is an oversimplification at the seed-emission level.
